story_type: C-130 air tankers low over a record wildfire
hook: A C-130 dropping retardant just over the treetops.
narration: This C-130 is laying a red line of retardant just over the treetops of the largest fire in California's history.
C-130s from the 146th Airlift Wing were called in to help CAL FIRE fight it.
The crews dipped down into canyons, flew through smoke, and buzzed the treetops.
One pilot put it plainly: at a hundred and fifty feet and a hundred and twenty knots, you are flying the airplane on the edge of its envelope.
The gear is called MAFFS. It slides into a C-130 and can be ready to fly in three hours.
For some of them, this was home. One could see the smoke from his own house.
[short pause] People in their own unit had lost places to live.
outcome: Back at the fire bases, ground crews black with ash gave them fist bumps for every load that came down.
title: C-130 at 150 feet over a wildfire
description:
C-130s of the 146th Airlift Wing flew Modular Airborne Fire Fighting System missions for CAL FIRE against the largest fire in California's history, around Ventura, California (released Jan. 2018).
